evidence.estrutura: Her peace movement built grassroots coalitions across communities rather than centralized political hierarchy; modest decentralist tendency.
evidence.representacao: Women’s participation in peacebuilding and public decision-making is central to her activism.
evidence.poder: Nonviolent mobilization against armed factions and coercive conflict strongly favors restraint on violence and civic pressure over force.
evidence.imigracao: Interfaith and cross-community organizing supports inclusive pluralism rather than cultural exclusion.
evidence.diplomacia: Her movement’s defining strategy was nonviolent pressure for negotiated peace, placing her strongly on the pacifist/diplomatic pole.
evidence.intervencao: Preference for locally driven peace and political settlement supports self-determination and non-intervention.
evidence.economia: Postwar peacebuilding includes women’s economic empowerment, but no full ownership-system doctrine; moderate-left development orientation.
evidence.controle: No command-planning doctrine; community development and public support imply moderate regulation.
evidence.religiao: Christian faith and deliberate Christian-Muslim cooperation make religion important personally while opposing sectarian rule.
evidence.moral: Women’s rights and interfaith peacebuilding strongly support egalitarian social values.
evidence.tecnologia: Technology was not a defining issue; moderate.
